summary: First test pass on the Supplier Portal buyer-entity (RI/RT) scoping feature (mrp vendor side changes.docx). Backend: 10/10 pytest checks pass (PO list buyer_code/buyer_entity_name, GRN lookup allowed_site_ids narrowing for RI/RT/legacy, 400 rejection of cross-entity site on approve, 403 for unbound site, 404/401 edges, P1 QC warehouse present). Frontend: verified single-entity vendor (H1330, all RI) sees the PO table immediately with no picker; seeded a temporary RT PO to make the vendor 2-entity and confirmed the entity switcher + 'Choose an entity to continue' blocking card, per-entity row filtering and cart clearing on entity switch; confirmed the Shipments edit dialog only offers same-entity (RI) items and zero cross-entity (RT) items; confirmed GRN Approval shows 'Buyer entity: <NAME>', narrows the Site dropdown to that entity's sites only (RI=P1,P8 / RT=P2,P2W,P3,P4,P7,P9), auto-locks (disabled) when one site qualifies, auto-preselects the site's -QC warehouse (P1-QC, P2-QC, P8-QC) while the Warehouse dropdown stays clickable with all 8 warehouses; legacy (no buyer_code) shipment still falls back to all sites with no entity line. Reject + Mark Discrepancy regressions pass. Approve-to-SAP was deliberately NOT executed (per instructions); the site/entity validation was proven via API with a wrong site_id. All seeded fixtures (2 po_cache rows, 4 shipments, 1 synthetic session/user) were deleted afterwards - verified zero residue.

minor.issue: Single-entity-per-shipment is enforced only in the UI. _resolve_items stores each line's buyer_code but never validates that all lines share one buyer_code, so a direct API call can still mix RI+RT items in one shipment; shipment_buyer_code() then silently returns the FIRST item's entity and GRN Approval would receive cross-entity lines under one site. Recommend raising ShipmentValidationError when resolved items span >1 buyer_code.

For a site-bound user whose bound_sites do not intersect the shipment's entity sites (verified: user bound to P3 only + RI shipment) the endpoint returns allowed_site_ids: [] with HTTP 200 and no explanatory flag - the UI then falls back to showing ALL sites (see frontend issue). Consider returning the entity's sites plus a separate 'not_bound' signal, or a 403-style message.

ui_bugs.issue: eligibleSites = shipment?.allowed_site_ids?.length ? filtered : sites - when the backend legitimately returns an EMPTY allowed_site_ids (site-bound user with no site in the shipment's entity, reproduced with a P3-bound user + RI shipment) the dropdown falls back to ALL 8 sites and no lock, i.e. the exact opposite of the intended restriction. Approve is still blocked backend-side (403/400) so there is no data corruption, but the screen is misleading. Should show a blocked state and disable Approve.

lookup() computes the auto-locked site from the `sites` state captured at call time; `sites` is loaded by a separate async loadSites() on mount. If a lookup resolves before the site list arrives (slow inventory call / deep-link + immediate lookup) eligibleSites is [] -> falls back to all sites and siteId stays empty, with no re-computation afterwards. Suggest deriving siteId in a useEffect on [shipment, sites].

issues: 'Bill Date' and the shipments From/To date filters use the browser-native date input (mm/dd/yyyy) instead of the shadcn calendar component used elsewhere - pre-existing, not part of this change

action_items: Enforce single buyer entity per shipment in supplier_shipment_service._resolve_items / create_shipment / update_shipment (backend), not just in the dashboard/edit UI
Fix GrnApprovalPage eligibleSites fallback so an EMPTY allowed_site_ids blocks the form instead of showing every site
Optional: recompute the auto-locked siteId in a useEffect on [shipment, sites] to remove the sites-not-yet-loaded race
critical_code_review_comments: supplier_shipment_service.prepare_approval correctly hard-blocks a cross-entity site (400 with entity name + valid site list) - verified live; but the equivalent guard is missing at shipment creation/edit time, so the invariant shipment_buyer_code() relies on ('every item shares one entity') is only UI-guaranteed.
GrnApprovalPage.jsx duplicates the eligible-sites derivation twice (inline `eligibleSites` const and again inside lookup()); extract one helper to avoid the two copies drifting.
GRN code input has maxLength 6, so any hand-seeded test shipment code longer than 6 chars cannot be looked up from the UI - worth noting for future fixtures (real codes are 6 chars).

Backend became completely unresponsive on port 8001 for ~4-5 minutes after every uvicorn --reload restart (any file write under /app/backend) - startup work appears to block the event loop before the app starts serving. Pre-existing, but it makes any edit under /app/backend cost several minutes of downtime.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the new-feature flows verified (2 non-blocking edge-case UI defects reported)

rca_of_the_issue: No functional defect found in the implemented feature itself. The two reported frontend defects share one root cause: `allowed_site_ids` is overloaded - it means both 'the entity's sites' and 'the entity's sites you are bound to', and an empty array (no overlap) is indistinguishable from 'unknown/legacy', so the UI's `length ? filter : sites` fallback opens the dropdown to every site. Backend prepare_approval + _has_site_access still reject such an attempt, so the impact is UI-only.
